cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a pair of reindeer-skin trouser leggings with dark wool cloth cuffs and tasselled cords, a classic Sámi garment type used for cold-weather herding dress. This matches well-documented Sámi material culture.

physical.title: trousers; legging
physical.summary:
A pair of man's (?) trouser leggings made of reindeer skin and cloth.  Tapered, with fur on the inside.  Tube formed of skin at top of leggings through which is threaded a plied cream skin cord with small pieces of red, yellow and blue cloth at each end, forming a tassel.  A 17 cms deep piece of dark blue tabby woven wool cloth with nap stitched to bottom of skin, with a narrow band of red cloth (felted wool ?) inside at the join. Parts of nap worn away; holes.  Some areas of sinew thread used to stitch strips of fur missing, leaving long rents in seams.
      They are inside out and too stiff now to turn the right way, but through some of the seams which have come apart, some of the external decoration is visible: about half way up the leg, a decorative panel formed of short lengths of skin alternating with red and blue felted wool strips are sewn into the seams. Each legging is made up of six strips of alternating light and dark fur each with a double strip gusset in between, the gussets also in alternating light and dark fur. The gathered top of the leggings through which the tie cord passes is made of a finer skin.
